ledger.x: c. 100: the Moche culture begins on the north coast of Peru. Infobox 'Established: 100 CE'; the culture 'flourished from about 100 to 800 AD' with Early (100-300), Middle (300-600) and Late (500-800) phases. The page calls it 'a group of autonomous polities that shared a common culture', not an empire.

c. 800: the Moche culture ends. Infobox 'Disestablished: 800 CE'; Moche polities survived beyond 650 in the Jequetepeque and Moche valleys; a possible 'super El Niño' c. 563-594 and inter-elite quarrelling are named as causes, and the page finds 'no evidence' of a Huari invasion. Heirs: Sicán in the north, Chimú in…

wars.name: Alleged Wari invasion of the Moche area
wars.outcome: The page says there is no evidence of a foreign invasion such as a Huari one; defensive works in the Jequetepeque valley point to unrest over scarce resources.

certainty.note: No borders: autonomous polities with a shared culture, drawn by valley.
